summary.text: Sedimentary rocks form when particles of minerals or organic matter that gathered at Earth's surface are cemented together.
They cover 73% of today's land surface, yet make up only about 8% of the volume of the crust.
Laid down in layers called strata, their sequence is the main source for understanding Earth's history, including the history of life.

facts.label: Resources
facts.value: Coal, fossil fuels, drinking water and ores

items.prompt: Sedimentary rock covers most of the land you walk on. Roughly what share of the crust's volume does it make up?
items.explain: Sedimentary rock covers 73% of the land but is only about 8% of the crust's volume, a thin veneer over igneous and metamorphic rock.

items.prompt: A rock is made of gravel whose pieces have sharp, angular edges. What is it called?
items.explain: Breccias are mostly angular gravel, while conglomerates are mostly rounded gravel.

items.prompt: Most limestone started out as what?

options.label: Lava that cooled on the seabed

items.explain: Most types of limestone form from the calcareous skeletons of organisms such as corals, mollusks and foraminifera.

items.prompt: A fast, muddy river slows down as it enters a still lake. What happens to its fine silt and clay?

options.label: They dissolve into the lake water
They speed up across the lake
They settle out as the water calms
They float on the surface forever

items.explain: Fine particles carried by turbulent flow are deposited as the flow calms and they settle out of suspension.

items.prompt: Why might engineers study the layers of sedimentary rock before digging a tunnel?

options.label: To date the age of the city

items.explain: Studying sedimentary rocks and strata gives information about the subsurface that is useful for building roads, tunnels and other structures.

items.prompt: Coal is a sedimentary rock. What was it before it was buried and transformed?

options.label: Sand blown in by the wind

items.explain: Coal forms from vegetation that is compressed by overlying sediments and chemically transformed.
